caption: Mean RGB value of the ROI crops per class and assay. Small differences between classes show how little colour contrast the network can exploit.

CNN backbones used (shared between the albumin and the creatinine branch). Trainable parameters are many times larger than the number of independent samples (100), which is why the recipe is strongly regularised and the evaluation strictly grouped by sample.

Strategy A (frozen ImageNet embeddings of both assays + logistic regression), nested CV, TEST level: mean ± SD over 10 outer folds, with the best classical model (SVM (RBF)) and the baselines for reference.
Strategy A: mean macro-F1 (test level, outer folds) using the albumin embedding only, the creatinine embedding only, or both. The bottom row is the best hand-crafted model (both assays).

Measurement audit with frozen CNN embeddings: sample-grouped cross-validated R² for predicting the laboratory analytes (and illumination) — 3 × 5-fold. The last row repeats the hand-crafted result of Path A for comparison (lux was not part of the Path A audit).
Strategy B (fine-tuned two-branch CNNs), nested evaluation on the identical outer folds, TEST level: mean ± SD over 10 folds, with the best classical model (SVM (RBF)) and the baselines.
Strategy B, SAMPLE level (repeat probabilities averaged before the decision). Secondary result.
All models on the identical outer folds, TEST level, sorted by mean macro-F1: mean ± SD over 10 outer folds.
All models, SAMPLE level (repeat probabilities averaged). Secondary result.

Each CNN-based model against the reference (SVM (RBF)): paired differences of fold-wise macro-F1 (test level), Wilcoxon and Nadeau–Bengio tests, Holm-corrected over 9 contrasts. Folds overlap, so the p-values are indicative.
Each CNN-based model against the two trivial baselines (paired Wilcoxon over folds, Holm-corrected). A model that is not better than the majority/random baseline has learned nothing transferable.
Pooled out-of-fold macro-F1 (repeat 1) with 95% cluster-bootstrap confidence intervals (1000 resamples of samples).
Paired cluster bootstrap of the difference in pooled out-of-fold macro-F1 between a CNN and the reference model (the same resampled samples are used for both, so the difference is paired).

Exploratory (post-hoc): average of the probabilities of the reference model and efficientnet_b0 (fine-tuned). Difference ensemble − reference: mean -0.006, Wilcoxon p = 0.846 (uncorrected, exploratory).

Diagnostic: macro-F1 at the pre-specified final epoch versus the best epoch chosen on the test folds (not allowed; shown to quantify the optimism). Rising test log-loss together with falling training loss indicates over-fitting.

Share of Grad-CAM mass in the outer frame of the crop (outer 20 % on each side) relative to its share of the area; 96 held-out tests of outer fold 1. A ratio clearly above 1 would indicate attention to the border.

Shortcut diagnostics for efficientnet_b0 (fine-tuned) on the held-out tests of outer fold 1: effect of brightness changes and of removing colour. Large changes under small brightness shifts indicate illumination sensitivity; little change after removing colour indicates that colour is not what the network uses.
